envelope.text: * **It does not sleep on RMW I/O.**

why:
rclrs drives spin_async on an async runtime (async-std/tokio). no_std targets have neither, and RFC-0002 puts one executor per RTOS task rather than a task-stealing runtime. The blocking `spin` is the whole model here.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded, argued rather than defaulted.

OURS EXISTS AND WORKS: `packages/core/nros-node/src/executor/spin.rs` (by name; the `:7114` this row cited has drifted), `pub async fn spin_async(&mut self) -> !` — `spin_once(1 ms)` then a `poll_fn` that calls `wake_by_ref` and returns `Pending`, forever. rclrs's is `spin_async(self, SpinOptions) -> impl Future<Output = Vec<RclrsError>>`.

WHY NOT REFUSE-LOUD: a refusal is a diagnostic naming the constraint; this name is a working entry point that the `Promise` pattern relies on (`select(executor.spin_async(), promise)`). Calling it refuse-loud claims a `compile_error!` that does not exist, and creating one means deleting a function that is the documented way to await a reply without an async runtime.

WHAT THE COMPILER POINTS AT: arity. Ours takes no options, so the ported `executor.spin_async(SpinOptions::default())` is `this method takes 0 arguments but 1 was supplied`; `rust:SpinOptions` and `rust:SpinOptions::until_promise_resolved` are absent, so every stop condition upstream expresses through options is a compile error here rather than an ignored value.

THE ENVELOPE, in the doc comment and restated here: (1) it never returns and reports no errors — `!`, not `Vec<RclrsError>`; a stop condition is expressed by `select`ing against the thing you are waiting for. (2) The yield is an ALWAYS-READY poll — `wake_by_ref` before `Pending` — so any runtime that honours wakes re-polls immediately: it is CPU-bound by construction, and the 1 ms `spin_once` budget is the only sleep in it. That is the no-runtime constraint made visible (RFC-0002: one executor per task, no task-stealing runtime to park on), not a bug; it is stated so a porting user does not read `async` as `idle`.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ROW CORRECTED, then the envelope WRITTEN. The paragraph above says the envelope is "in the doc comment and restated here"; it was not — the doc said only "Runs forever, yielding between poll cycles", which reads as idle, and `book/src/concepts/ros2-comparison.md` said `spin_async` "wakes on RMW I/O", the opposite of the code. The doc comment now states both bounds (never returns / no errors / no `SpinOptions`; the always-ready self-waking poll, CPU-bound, 1 ms `spin_once` its only wait), and the book's sentence is corrected.
